speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned an episode of loss of consciousness; can you describe exactly what happened leading up to that moment?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: That loss of consciousness occurring immediately after urination is a very specific detail; did you experience any chest pain, palpitations, or severe back pain just before you fainted? Also, have you noticed any difficulty starting your urine stream or a feeling of incomplete emptying?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episode of loss of consciousness. I also have Regained consciousness quickly without confusion, No urinary incontinence, No bite marks or injuries.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-Micturition Syncope.

This condition is a reflex vasovagal faint triggered by urination. Based on your rapid recovery and lack of injuries, I do not suspect cardiac arrest or trauma, but I would like to confirm your heart rhythm and check for structural issues.

REQUEST TEST: Electrocardiogram (ECG).
REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram.
